## TL;DR

I completed the Inputs and Context QA pass at desktop and phone widths with
headless Playwright against the auth-less task worktree server. The pages fit at
1280px and 375px, the screenshot picker and preview worked without submitting a
test record, and all four Context tabs loaded without horizontal overflow. The
pass exposed a real state-reporting bug: failed list requests could look like
successful empty results. Inputs and Context now show retryable errors and
distinguish loading, failure, and a genuine empty response. The first review
found one evidence gap: the handoff screenshots were at 1024px. I fixed the
capture plan to declare both routes at the requested 1280px and 375px widths.

## Work and rationale

I started from the task's acceptance criteria and ran `just serve-noauth 7272`
inside this task worktree. The server build completed and identified itself as
a preview. I used Playwright Chromium in headless mode; no visible browser or
main-checkout files were opened. The initial browse covered Inputs list and
board modes, an input detail drawer, the New input screenshot picker and
preview, and the Context Docs, Skills, Discover, and History tabs at 1280 × 900
and 375 × 900. I selected a small PNG to confirm the preview appeared and
removed it from the draft. I did not submit an input, create a document, or
install a skill, so the pass left no test content in the project.

Responsive checks found the document width equal to the viewport at both
target sizes. Inputs list and board, the detail drawer, and the screenshot
picker fit at 375px. Context remained within the viewport on all four tabs.
Existing documents appeared in the tree and selected content rendered in the
preview. No uncaught page errors or console errors occurred during normal use.

The initial failure simulations exposed two empty-state problems. The Inputs
store caught network errors without returning a result, leaving its empty
initial list in place; the page then said “No inputs here yet.” The docs store
did return `false` when `/api/docs` failed, but Context ignored that result and
showed “No docs found” while loading or after failure. Both messages implied
there was no content when the request had not succeeded.

I changed `refreshInputs()` to return whether the latest fetch succeeded while
preserving existing input data on error. Inputs now displays an error and Retry
action in both list and board modes. A successful retry clears the error and
returns to the real results or empty state. The docs store now exposes its
loading and error state. Context shows “Loading docs…” during the request, an
error with Retry after failure, and “No docs found” only after a successful
empty response. The docs refresh button uses the same store path, so initial
loading and manual refresh stay consistent.

The first review found no code defects. It found that my declared handoff shots
were captured at 1024 × 768 by default and did not prove the stated acceptance
widths. I checked the shot-plan parser and added explicit viewport width and
height fields to four captures: Inputs at 1280 × 900 and 375 × 812, and Context
at those same two sizes. The handoff will now capture the actual desktop and
phone widths instead of relying only on separate local screenshots. The QA
note records this correction.

## Approaches tried

I first exercised the pages with ordinary worktree data, then checked their
scroll widths at both target viewport sizes. The file-picker exercise covered
selection and preview while avoiding a persistent input record. For error
states, I intercepted the list API calls and returned 503 responses. The first
probe let a second background Inputs fetch succeed before I checked the page,
so the error disappeared too quickly. I adjusted the route to hold every
matching request at 503 until Retry was pressed. That made the failure and
recovery states deterministic. Inputs recovered to its data after retry, and
Context recovered to its document tree.

I added focused regression coverage to the Inputs view and docs store. The
Inputs test checks that a failed load displays the error instead of the
successful-empty message, and that Retry clears the alert. The docs-store test
checks failure state, loading completion, and error clearing after a successful
retry. The configured `bun run test` wrapper passed the focused tests and its
boot-timing pass; a direct Vitest invocation was not appropriate because it
bypassed the repository's Vue SFC plugin setup.

After the initial handoff, I read the newest review report. Its sole finding was
the capture-width evidence gap. The shot-plan schema supports per-shot
`viewportWidth` and `viewportHeight`, so I updated the task's declared shots
instead of changing the app or relaxing the acceptance criteria. Each of the
two pages now has an explicitly sized desktop shot and phone shot, with a
highlight selector that exists on its route.

## Challenges and blockers

There was no product or repository blocker. The first browser failure probe
waited for an error while another request had already succeeded. Inspecting the
request traffic showed why it happened, and holding all matching requests
until the explicit retry fixed the probe. Direct Vitest initially failed before
loading the Vue view; the repository's configured test wrapper then ran the
affected tests successfully. These were harness adjustments, not unresolved
failures.

The simulated 503 responses generated expected browser resource-error messages.
They came from the deliberate network interception, not uncaught application
exceptions. The normal flow and successful retry flows produced no uncaught
page errors. Local QA screenshots are under the task worktree's ignored
`.repoos/qa-1204/` directory.

## Key learnings

An empty-state check needs to separate a request still in progress, a failed
request, and a successful response with no data. An initial empty array alone
cannot represent all three. The store needs to expose request outcome so the
view can show useful guidance, and failure should preserve data that was
already loaded. The Inputs change follows that rule without clearing its list;
the docs store exposes shared status for both initial load and manual refresh.

Failure probes also need to control concurrent and background requests. The
first transient 503 was hidden by a second fetch, while a deterministic route
held the error visible until a deliberate retry. Finally, a manual responsive
pass and handoff evidence are different artifacts: the first pass checked
1280px and 375px locally, but the default capture viewport recorded 1024px.
Making viewport dimensions part of each declared screenshot ensures reviewers
see the sizes required by the task.

The scoped RepoOS check passed formatting, lint, build, UI guards, rendered
contrast, browser smoke, and the remote changed-path suite of 1,705 tests.
RepoOS created its own WIP checkpoint for validation; I did not stage or commit
files manually.
